questions.q: What is the correct HTML tag for the highest-level heading in a document, and how many levels of headings does HTML provide?
questions.a: The correct tag is `<h1>` and HTML provides six levels (`<h1>` through `<h6>`). A wrong answer like `<heading>` or `<h0>` reveals the student doesn't know the exact tag syntax; answering "7 levels" or "unlimited" shows confusion about the fixed hierarchy defined by the HTML specification.

questions.q: Explain the difference between `<b>` and `<strong>` tags. They both make text bold visually — so why does HTML have both?
questions.a: `<b>` is a presentational tag that only specifies bold styling without semantic meaning, while `<strong>` indicates strong importance/seriousness/urgency. Screen readers may announce `<strong>` with emphasis but ignore `<b>`; search engines weight `<strong>` content higher for relevance. A student who says "they are the same" misses the core concept of semantic vs. presentational markup.

questions.q: Write the HTML code to display the chemical formula for glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and a footnote reference like "See note²" where the "2" is superscript.
questions.a: Correct code: `C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>` and `See note<sup>2</sup>`. A student writing `<sub>6</sub>` without the element name (e.g., `C<sub>6</sub>`) shows they understand subscript but not that the tag wraps only the subscripted characters. Using `<sup>2</sup>` for the footnote is correct; using `<sup>See note 2</sup>` would incorrectly superscript the whole phrase.

questions.q:
A webpage has this structure: `

Fruits

Apples

Vegetables

Carrots

`. Identify two problems with this heading hierarchy and explain why they hurt accessibility.
questions.a: Problem 1: Skipping from `<h1>` to `<h3>` (missing `<h2>`) breaks the logical outline — screen reader users navigating by headings will jump from level 1 to level 3, missing level 2 context. Problem 2: `<h4>` appears under `<h2>` but there is no `<h3>` between them, creating an inconsistent hierarchy. Both violate the rule that heading levels must increase by at most 1 and never skip levels downward.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "Since `<i>` and `<em>` both render as italic text in browsers, they are interchangeable. Use whichever is shorter to type." Defend your position with two concrete reasons.
questions.a: The statement is false. Reason 1: `<em>` conveys *stress emphasis* (affects screen reader intonation), while `<i>` only indicates *alternate voice/mood* (e.g., taxonomic names, foreign words) without emphasis. Reason 2: SEO crawlers treat `<em>` as a signal of important keywords; `<i>` carries no such weight. Using `<i>` for emphasis harms accessibility and search ranking.
